evals.prompt:
/verifiable:paths src/board.ts

its the function that builds the text for our bus stop boards. i want to know if the tests we need for it can even be counted before i spend time on it
evals.expected_output: A read-only report: no project file is changed. It gives the exits and branch points that diagnose printed for boardText, names each open branch with what it depends on (the stop text, the line number, the timetable call), mentions the catch that merges every failure into one value, and gives no invented number of tests.

evals.prompt:
/verifiable:coverage src/board.ts

boardText is the thing that decides what a bus stop board shows. requirement as far as i know it: a stop id is two capital letters, a dash, three digits. lines run 1 to 99. if the timetable has no service for the line (it throws NoService) the board says 'no service', anything else going wrong should just blow up. a bus that is due or already there shows 'due', up to and including 60 minutes shows the minutes, more shows 'more than an hour'. go ahead and do the whole thing, the project folder is a throwaway copy already
evals.expected_output: The code is reshaped into the shapes with a verifiable.json, the inventory prints no REJECTED line and wrote an obligations file, one spec per unit exists and starts with the requirement, the computed checks pass through an entry file, the existing tests still pass, a reconciliation was run, only skipped tests were removed without further selection and each is listed with its evidence; tests with the verdict cannot fail on the counted code are kept pending review of their remaining purpose and explicit user selection, and the report marks lines Run or Read, says what is outside the claim, and lists the specs a person has to review. No test case was written by hand for code in the shapes.

evals.prompt:
/verifiable:paths Decision.cs

Can the checks for this borrowing decision be counted? Keep the source and specs unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Selects the C# backend; builds in temporary storage if needed; runs its paths command and reports four Boolean combinations for Example.Decision.CanBorrow. States that no specs or methods were executed, the scope is this standalone file, and application build settings were not loaded. Does not invoke the TypeScript inventory.

evals.prompt:
/verifiable:coverage Decision.cs

This is a throwaway copy. A copy can be borrowed only when it is available and the borrower is not suspended. Check that requirement using the supplied spec.
evals.expected_output: Uses the C# subset, computes the inventory and runs fresh compiled-method checks. Reports four passing checks only if observed, names the spec for independent review, says application build/test evidence is absent unless separately run, and marks reconciliation unavailable. Does not remove tests or claim the complete coverage workflow passed.

evals.prompt:
/verifiable:prune Decision.cs

The C# checks pass. Please remove redundant tests based on that result.
evals.expected_output: Explains that C# reconciliation and pruning are unsupported, and passing computed checks do not establish redundancy. Leaves tests unchanged; does not invoke the TypeScript mutation or prune tools.
